sections.overview: This small montane rattlesnake is native to west-central Mexico, chiefly the highlands of Michoacán and adjacent Jalisco.
sections.identification: Adults are usually about half a metre long, with a gray-brown ground colour and darker dorsal blotches.
sections.habitat: It occupies high-elevation pine-oak forest and rocky volcanic or limestone slopes.
sections.diet: Lizards form its main known prey, including Sceloporus and Barisia; one report also records a bat.
sections.behavior: It is a ground-dwelling ambush predator of rocky highlands; detailed activity patterns are not well documented.
sections.reproduction: A published observation reports a small litter, but the species’ reproductive biology remains poorly known.
sections.ecology: It shares Mexico’s volcanic highlands with Crotalus intermedius, but belongs to a different rattlesnake species group.
sections.conservation: The Mexican rattlesnake action plan describes a restricted montane distribution and identifies local records for conservation planning.
